requirements.semantic_review: F061 checked against the chosen transport: one TCP listening socket whose byte stream supplies the ordered, lossless byte ordering the protocol needs, driven by a single-threaded epoll reactor in src/loop.c. module_spec CR-BUILD/CR-READY/CR-MODE inspected: net_listen uses socket(AF_INET,SOCK_STREAM,0)+SO_REUSEADDR+bind(INADDR_ANY,port)+listen, main rejects a missing/invalid argv[1] through net_parse_port and exits nonzero, loop_run loops on epoll_wait with LOOP_WAIT_MS and never performs a blocking operation on any peer (EAGAIN on read/write returns to the loop, mask_sync re-arms EPOLLIN/EPOLLOUT), so one slow or idle client cannot stall another. Verified: ./mqtt_broker <port> usage string and README content match the planned files and Makefile target names in module_spec FILES/GENERATION_ORDER. Domain checked is the full requested one (many concurrent clients, no per-peer threads); no narrowing and no correction required.

F008,F009,F010,F011,F012,F013,F014,F015,F016,F017,F021,F022,F023,F024 checked against wire_decode_connect and handle_connect decision order: CONNECT only as first packet (broker_process_input returns WIRE_INVALID for anything before CONNECT and for a second CONNECT, F008); byte 1 must be 0x10 (measured 0x10 = type 1<<4 | flags 0, F009) else silent close; protocol name must be 4D 51 54 54 with level 04 (F010) else CONNACK 20 02 00 01 then close; client id must be present, nonempty, well-formed UTF-8 (F014/F046): empty or out-of-charset ids are rejected with CONNACK 20 02 00 02 and close (F016, permitted because F014's longer/other-charset support and F015's empty-id support are MAY), reserved connect-flag bit 0, Will flag set, CleanSession=0 or a wrong protocol name close silently without CONNACK (F011/F017/F024). Success path builds CONNACK 20 02 00 00 with ack flags 00 (Session Present 0 for CleanSession=1, F022) and return code 00 (F017/F023). Early-return precedence was re-derived: level!=4 (mandatory rc 0x01) is evaluated before client-id checks (broker.c TEST_VECTORS/1: level 3 + empty id -> rc 1, not rc 2) and ill-formed UTF-8 closes silently instead of producing rc 0x02. Correction applied: files/src/broker.c.json#/TEST_VECTORS/2 case_0 used client-id bytes 41 ff 42 (ill-formed UTF-8) while expecting CONNACK 20 02 00 02; per F046 that input must close silently, so the case now uses 41 c3 a9 42 (well-formed non-ASCII 'A\u00e9B') for the rc 0x02 path and keeps e0 80 41 / 41 c0 80 42 as the silent-close cases. Duplicate CONNECT closes only that client (F008) and an already-connected session with the same client id is evicted (F017, handle_connect -> remove_session_at).

F033,F034,F036,F037,F038,F039,F040,F041,F007,F006 checked against handle_subscribe: fixed-header flags must be exactly 0x2 (F033) else close; packet id must be nonzero 2-byte MSB-first (F006); payload is a list of >=1 UTF-8 filter + requested-QoS pairs, upper 6 bits of the QoS byte reserved (F034), a filter is rejected when its reserved bits are set, the payload is empty, or the QoS byte is not 0/1/2. Response is one SUBACK 90 (2+n) pid_msb pid_lsb code[0..n-1] with the SUBSCRIBE's own packet id (F007/F036) and one ordered return code per filter (F037/F040). Grant derivation: the broker only serves QoS 0 and always answers 0x00 (F038 success maximum QoS 0), which is F041-legal because the server may grant a lower maximum QoS than requested. Corrections applied: files/src/broker.c.json#/TEST_VECTORS/6 expected codes 02,01 (granting the requested QoS 2/1) although handle_subscribe passes GRANTED_QOS 0 to session_add_subscription; renamed to subscribe_two_filters_grants_qos0_in_order and set EXPECT 90 04 00 0a 00 00 with code_0=0, code_1=0 (input still requests QoS 2 and 1, so the vector now demonstrates the permitted lower grant). TEST_VECTORS/7 likewise re-expects 90 03 00 01 00 / 90 03 00 02 00 with stored_qos 0, and files/src/session.c.json#/TEST_VECTORS/4 third call now stores qos 0 so no stored subscription claims a maximum QoS the broker cannot deliver. Identical filters replace in place (F039/F040) with the count staying 2 in that vector.

F025,F026,F028,F030,F032,F062,F063,F064 checked against handle_publish and route_publish: an inbound QoS 0 PUBLISH has no packet identifier (F006) so the variable header is only the topic name; the broker keeps the received topic name and the payload bytes and, for every connected session whose subscription matches, queues an outbound PUBLISH with type 3, DUP=0 (F026/F062), QoS 0 and RETAIN=0 because delivery is due to an established subscription (F028). Independent length derivations, all recomputed and asserted: topic 't' + payload 'v' -> RL 2+1+1 = 4, bytes 30 04 00 01 74 76; topic 'sport/tennis/score' (18 bytes) + 2-byte payload -> 00 12 and RL 22, bytes 30 16 00 12 ..; topic 'alerts/fire' (11 bytes) + payload 00 01 -> 00 0B and RL 15, total frame 17 bytes. Every matching session gets an independent copy (F063/F064) and a non-matching session's queue stays empty; the publisher's own matching subscription also receives it (loopback). Payload bytes are copied verbatim including NULs; the outbound topic is byte-identical to the inbound one (F056 no normalization).

F050,F051,F052,F053,F054,F055,F056 checked against topic_filter_matches/topic_filter_validate/topic_name_validate: levels are split on '/' with adjacent separators producing zero-length levels (F051), '#' is allowed alone or after a separator as the final character and matches the parent level and any number of child levels including zero (F052), '+' must occupy a whole level and matches exactly one level (F053), matching is case-sensitive character-for-character with no normalization (F055/F056), and a filter whose first level starts with '#' or '+' must not match a topic name beginning with '$' (F054). Derived case table replayed element by element against the saved match array: 'sport/tennis/player1/#' vs 'sport/tennis/player1' true (# covers zero levels), 'sport/#' vs 'sport' true, 'sport/+' vs 'sport/' true (empty level is one level), '+/+' vs '/finance' true (two levels, first empty), '# ' vs 'a/b/c' true, '+/monitor/Clients' and '#' vs '$SYS/..' false (F054) while '$SYS/#' vs '$SYS/x' true, 'sport/+' vs 'sport/tennis/player1' false, 'a//b' vs 'a//b' true. Correction applied: files/src/topic.c.json#/TEST_VECTORS/5 index 7 ['+','/finance'] was expected true but '/finance' has two levels ('', 'finance') per F051 so a single '+' cannot match; EXPECT/match[7] is now false and the contrast pair ['+','finance'] -> true was appended (array lengths equal 18). Wildcard filters are supported outright, not rejected (F035 supported class).

F030,F045,F047,F049 checked: the PUBLISH payload is carried as an explicit (pointer,length) borrowed slice (wire_decode_publish) and copied with memcpy of that length into each subscriber's output queue, so no NUL termination or C-string operation is involved and a zero-length payload is a valid message (F030). Independent lengths: zero-length payload leaves RL = 2 + topic_len (e.g. topic 't' -> RL 3, frame 30 03 00 01 74); payload 'v' -> RL 4; a 2-byte payload 00 01 -> RL 2+topic_len+2. The U+0000 prohibition of F047 is applied only to UTF-8 encoded strings that the protocol encodes as strings (protocol name, client id, topic name/filter via topic_utf8_validate), not to payload bytes, which is why payloads containing 00 are routed byte-exactly; the 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF sequence is likewise not stripped anywhere (F049) and the decoder never scans payload content for it. Vectors replayed: payload containing NUL, empty payload, and binary payloads of length >1 with the exact wire bytes above; no correction required.

F001,F004,F005,F058,F059 checked against wire_decode_header/wire_read_remaining_length and pump_read: the fixed header is byte 1 (type in bits 7-4, flags 3-0) followed by the Remaining Length starting at byte 2 (F001); decoding accumulates value += (b & 127) * multiplier with multipliers 1,128,16384,2097152 and reports malformed only when the fourth byte still has the continuation bit set, i.e. multiplier > 128^3 (F005), which also rejects the over-long 5-byte form. Widths recomputed and asserted: 0->1 byte, 127->1 byte, 128->80 01, 16383->FF 7F, 16384->80 80 01, 268435455->FF FF FF 7F (F004 max_wire_bytes). Outcomes: WIRE_INCOMPLETE consumes nothing and the bytes stay buffered for the next read; WIRE_COMPLETE reports packet_len = fixed-header bytes + RL value and consumed = that total; WIRE_INVALID covers reserved types 0/15, the F003 invalid-flag table, malformed RL and truncated packets. The session input buffer keeps partial frames between reads and pump_read processes every coalesced frame in the same loop pass in arrival order. Correction applied earlier and re-checked: wire_decode_empty now accepts every legal encoding of value 0 (C0 80 00 / C0 80 80 00 / C0 80 80 80 00) with consumed 3/4/5 because F004/F005 define no minimal-length rule, while nonzero RL, flags != 0, wrong type and an incomplete 5-byte continuation are invalid; files/src/wire.c.json#/TEST_VECTORS/10 was updated to COMPLETE,COMPLETE,COMPLETE with consumed 3,3,5 then INVALID,INVALID,INVALID. Second correction: files/src/broker.c.json#/TEST_VECTORS/13 used the bare 'c0 01' input, which is merely INCOMPLETE and must not close; the case is now the complete frame 'c0 01 00' (RL 1 != 0, WIRE_INVALID) and does close.

F025,F058,F062 checked against pump_read and broker_session_eof: on read() returning 0 the loop does not discard the buffer contents first; every complete frame already accumulated in the session input buffer is decoded and dispatched in order before the connection is torn down, and only a trailing incomplete frame is dropped with the connection (matching 'CONNECT may be followed immediately by further control packets', F025). This makes the required final-PUBLISH-then-shutdown case work: the publisher's last frame is routed to subscribers, whose queues are flushed by the loop independently of anything the subscriber sends, and then the publisher session is closed. Independent replay: publish 't'/'v' (frame 30 04 00 01 74 76) followed by shutdown(SHUT_WR) on the publisher produces exactly one subscriber PUBLISH 30 04 00 01 74 76 and no error on the subscriber; bytes '30 04 00 01 74' (incomplete) followed by EOF produce no PUBLISH and a clean close; the broker keeps accepting new clients afterwards (state effect limited to the closing connection, F058).

F042,F043 checked against handle_pingreq and wire_encode_pingresp: PINGREQ is type 12 (12<<4 = 0xC0, fixed-header flags 0) with Remaining Length 0 (F042); the response is exactly D0 00 (13<<4 = 0xD0, RL 0, F043) and the session stays SESSION_READY with no state change, so a later SUBSCRIBE or PUBLISH on the same connection is still processed (confirmed by the sequential vector ping -> publish -> suback). Any other Remaining Length or fixed-header flag value for PINGREQ is WIRE_INVALID and closes that connection only. Keep-alive expiry scheduling is deliberately absent (excluded by scope R09): the 16-bit Keep Alive field is decoded by wire_decode_connect and stored/ignored by handle_connect (F018), and no timer path exists, so no interval boundary can cause a disconnect. Correction applied: files/src/broker.c.json#/TEST_VECTORS/13's third case used the bare 'c0 01' (incomplete frame, would not close) and now uses the complete frame 'c0 01 00'.

F008,F012,F017,F044,F060,F064,F066 checked against handle_disconnect, broker_process_input, broker_reap and session_destroy: DISCONNECT is type 14 with flags 0 and RL 0 (F044) and is accepted only from a READY session; on receipt the session's subscriptions are released (free_subscriptions), its state becomes SESSION_CLOSED, queued output is discarded (session_close_immediately) and no Will is published (none can exist because CONNECT with Will is rejected). EOF from the peer reaches the same teardown through broker_session_eof. Resources: the session object leaves the poll registration (is_registered guards a later event in the same batch), and broker_reap/session_destroy frees the subscription entries, the client-id copy, the input buffer and the output queue; other sessions' state is untouched. Stale-subscription check: every new connection is created with sub_count 0 and an empty subscription list and CleanSession is always 1 in scope, so the state is discarded and never reused in a later session (F012, scope-supported because F014/F015 optional session resumption is out of the accepted domain); reconnecting the same client id later yields sub_count 0 and no PUBLISH is routed to it. Same-id takeover evicts the previous READY session through remove_session_at before the new one is registered (F017).

F002,F003,F005,F006,F011,F019,F025,F027,F029,F033,F034,F042,F044,F046,F047,F050,F055,F058,F059 checked against the validators. Malformed/unframeable class (silent close of that connection, F058, no CONNACK): reserved types 0 and 15 (F002); flags differing from the F003 table (CONNECT 0, PUBACK/PUBREC/PUBREL/PUBCOMP/SUBACK/UNSUBACK/PINGREQ/PINGRESP/DISCONNECT per table, SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE 2); PUBLISH with QoS bits 11 (F027); malformed/truncated Remaining Length (F005); CONNECT reserved connect-flag bit set (F011), Will flag set or Will QoS 3 (F019), CleanSession 0, protocol level != 4, ill-formed UTF-8 or U+0000 in any string field (F046/F047); non-CONNECT first packet and any data after a rejected CONNECT (F025); SUBSCRIBE pid 0 (F006), empty payload, payload reserved bit or QoS 3 (F034); PUBLISH topic containing '+' or '#' (F029/F050) or a zero/oversized topic (F055); PINGREQ/DISCONNECT with RL != 0 or flags != 0 (F042/F044). Well-formed but unsupported class: packet types outside the in-scope set (PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP, UNSUBSCRIBE, UNSUBACK) and PUBLISH with QoS 1 or 2 are recognized as protocol-correct frames but outside the implemented feature set; they close only the offending connection and are never answered with a SUBACK/PUBACK-style reply (F024/F059 semantics for an unsupported request), so a mandatory rejection such as QoS 3 (F027) is never masked by the generic unsupported policy because the QoS-bit test runs first. Isolation invariant: only the offending session is closed and freed, the listener and every other session continue (F059), covered by broker.c TEST_VECTORS/8 (SUBSCRIBE failures, other_sessions_unaffected true) and the invalid-header vectors. No scope narrowing found in the accepted input domain for CONNECT/SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH QoS 0/PINGREQ/DISCONNECT.

F004,F058,F059,F062 checked as ownership across repeated legal operations. Allocation map: session_input buffer is owned by the session, grown with realloc by buffer_reserve (temporary old pointer, freed only when the realloc fails) and freed in session_destroy; topic/payload slices returned by wire_decode_* borrow the input buffer and are consumed before any compaction or reallocation because handle_publish copies the bytes into each subscriber's queue (route_publish -> session_enqueue) inside the same dispatch. session_output queue is owned by the session: buffer_reserve must not leak the previous pointer when growing, buffer_commit/consume keep unsent bytes, and net_write_some partial writes keep the remainder queued with EPOLLOUT still armed (mask_sync) so an idle recipient still receives queued output. Subscriptions: session_add_subscription owns one malloc'd copy per filter and reuses the existing slot in place for an identical filter, so no old filter is leaked or double freed on re-subscribe (verified in session.c TEST_VECTORS/4, count stays 2 with the third call replacing 'a/b' in place); session_destroy/free_subscriptions releases every copy, the client-id copy and both buffers. Repeated-operation paths checked: subscribe twice with the same filter, re-CONNECT with the same client id (old session freed by remove_session_at), and two successive publishes of different lengths on one connection (queue grown, not leaked). Termination: the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler (on_signal) only sets a sig_atomic_t flag; loop_run observes it, returns 0, and main then stops the loop and destroys the broker/sessions/queues and closes the listening descriptor, so all resources are released outside the handler. No ASan/UBSan evidence is required or claimed, matching R12's exclusion.

processing_chain.description: net_listen creates the nonblocking listener; loop_run sees data.ptr NULL and calls accept_ready, which accepts a bounded burst through net_accept and hands each nonblocking, close-on-exec descriptor to broker_accept/add_session, so every new connection starts as an AWAITING_CONNECT session with empty buffers that mask_sync registers for EPOLLIN.

pump_read appends recv bytes into the session input buffer and broker_process_input repeatedly frames one packet with wire_decode_header, dispatches to the CONNECT/SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH/PINGREQ/DISCONNECT handler and consumes exactly header total_len; INCOMPLETE leaves the tail buffered, INVALID closes only that session.

handle_connect rejects a non-CONNECT-first or duplicate CONNECT target, stores the client id copy through session_set_client_id, queues the exact 20 02 00 00 CONNACK, marks the session READY and evicts an older READY session with the same identifier; unsupported level or identifier gets return code 1/2 then close-after-flush.

handle_subscribe walks the validated filter list with wire_subscribe_next, replaces or appends each QoS 0 subscription through session_add_subscription and queues one SUBACK whose variable part echoes the nonzero Packet Identifier and holds one 0x00 code per filter in order.

handle_publish rejects QoS 1/2 and DUP-at-QoS-0 by closing the publisher, otherwise route_publish encodes one QoS 0 PUBLISH from a private scratch buffer and enqueues it to every READY session whose stored filters match the topic (publisher included); only a recipient whose enqueue fails is closed, and mask_sync then arms EPOLLOUT for the queued recipients.
handle_pingreq queues the exact two-byte PINGRESP through session_output, leaving the READY state and all other queued bytes untouched so business traffic continues.

broker_session_eof processes every complete buffered frame first (including a final PUBLISH followed by write-side shutdown), leaves an incomplete tail discarded, moves the session to CLOSING with its queued output preserved; pump_write drains it, broker_reap closes and destroys drained sessions, and handle_disconnect closes immediately without flushing.

on_signal only stores 1 into the sig_atomic_t flag; loop_run observes the flag or loop_stop and returns, then main tears down in order loop_destroy, net_close_fd(&listener), broker_destroy, so every session descriptor, buffer, copied identifier, subscription and array is released.

engineering_decisions.reason: Framing returns an explicit three-way status (INCOMPLETE/COMPLETE/INVALID) plus the exact frame length instead of a byte count, so the caller can keep a partial tail buffered, consume a complete frame precisely and close only the offending connection on malformed input (R07, R11).

CONNECT decoding keeps every length-prefixed field as a borrowed (pointer,length) span into the caller's packet buffer, so field text is never copied and the decoder performs no allocation (R02, R12).

Every heap object a session keeps (input storage, output storage, client identifier, subscription copies) is owned by exactly one session object and released by session_destroy, which gives the registry a single cleanup point (R12).
An identical stored filter is replaced in place and a new filter is appended, so a repeated SUBSCRIBE neither leaks the previous copy nor duplicates the subscription (F039, F040, R03).

The broker registry owns an array of session pointers plus one reusable scratch buffer; route_publish encodes once into the scratch buffer and enqueues per recipient, so a fan-out has no per-recipient heap churn and the scratch storage is reused across messages (R04, R12).

The publisher is included in the recipient scan and only a recipient whose enqueue fails is closed, so the fan-out is isolated per connection and one failing peer cannot stop delivery to the others (R04, R11, F057).

Descriptor modes are established where the descriptors are created (SOCK_NONBLOCK|SOCK_CLOEXEC for the listener, accept plus fcntl(F_SETFL,O_NONBLOCK) and fcntl(F_SETFD,FD_CLOEXEC) for peers) and the readiness loop dispatches a read only for EPOLLIN/RDHUP/HUP/ERR on an AWAITING_CONNECT or READY session and a write only for EPOLLOUT/HUP/ERR while READY/CLOSING output remains, so a writable-only event never triggers a blocking read and queued output still reaches an idle recipient (R01, R11).
Signal handlers only set a sig_atomic_t flag, so every buffer, descriptor and session is released by ordinary code in main after loop_run returns rather than inside a handler (R12).
